question.text: If a Cat III AIF treats shares as 'Investments' (not stock-in-trade), dividends received are taxable as:

answer.text: Income from Other Sources (with 20% interest-expenditure deduction only)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 9.3.2, dividends from shares held as 'Investments' are taxed as 'Income from Other Sources'; only interest expenditure up to 20% of dividend is deductible. The Trap: Classifying under Business requires stock-in-trade treatment; exemption doesn't exist post-2020. Cross-Exam Context: Critical characterization impacting deductions. Distributor's Pro-Tip: The stock-in-trade vs investment election is a strategic choice — review with tax advisor annually.
